newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia 1997 net grain harvest still seen 70 mln T.
newsitem.headline: Russia 1997 net grain harvest still seen 70 mln T.

text.p: Russia's Agriculture Minister Viktor Khlystun forecast on Tuesday a net grain harvest of 70 million tonnes this year, adhering to previous government forecasts.
"Seventy million tonnes is the prediction, and this is realistic," he said. "But I hope it will be bigger."
Asked about Russia's grain import needs this year, Khlystun said -- "We will not do centralised imports," referring to imports by the government.
"We will be fully supplied with food wheat and won't need to buy, but will need maize." He gave no volumes for the maize imports.
He put Russian food grain imports over the 1995/96 crop year at 4.0 to 4.5 million tonnes.

Private commodity houses have been gradually importing grains to Russia, as the government loosens its grip on the market. Russia's net grain harvest last year was 69.3 million tonnes, the second worst on record in three decades.
